title: Invocation grammar designed with Sameer: name-addressing, spawn flavours, deaf delivery

brief.why:
Discovered while working son-sireto (2026-08-09). Three grammar gaps measured live: (1) repo addressing rings the newest session in the subtree — ringing /home/modha to reach the phone rc session modha-7a would actually target a deeper repo session; hitting it needed a hand-rolled python deliver. No name-addressing exists. (2) A Vertex spawn cannot reuse spawn() as-is: claudefv is a commons-managed shell FUNCTION (bash -ic or env replication needed), and readiness must key on the registry record appearing — a Vertex session never binds the socket spawn() polls, so today it would burn the full 180s and fail. (3) Delivery to a deaf session has no peer route at all; candidate fallback is wake-or-file — durable message written to a file, spawn prompt carrying only a pointer — which bends the spawn-then-deliver convention and needs Sameer's explicit verdict, not a Claude's.

UPDATE 2026-08-09 ~21:55 (live rc experiment, evidence in ~/.claude/logs/claude-remote-home-modha.log): (4) Peer delivery into an iOS remote-control session works and is peer-framed; arriving MID-TASK it queues and never gets a turn after the task completes; arriving IDLE it WAKES the session, which acts and completes a turn. (5) The from-address gap is now measured from the receiving end: the woken session could not resolve script:sonner-3d (deaf sender = no reply address), so it GUESSED and misdelivered its ack to infra-signboard-46 — picked because that session lives in a tmux session named sonner-infra-signboard. Our own sonner-<repo> tmux naming is a decoy for peer reply-routing. Grammar needs: an honest no-reply marking for deaf senders (or a real reply route), and spawn tmux names that do not masquerade as sonner itself.
brief.what: 1. Draft grammar proposal (verbs, addressing forms, deaf-delivery fallback) 2. Decision session with Sameer 3. File implementation actions from the agreed design
brief.done: Grammar agreed with Sameer; implementation actions filed on this board reflecting the decisions.
brief.how: Bring a proposal to react to, not an open question: draft the verb set (ring = current; wake = spawn-only, no delivery; --name addressing beside repo addressing; --spawn-cmd or billing flavour for Vertex) with the wake-or-file compromise spelled out. Decide with Sameer, then file implementation actions from the agreed grammar.

title: sonner tells a deaf session from an empty repo — and never spawns a sibling silently

brief.why:
Measured 2026-08-09 on a live Vertex session (pid 88204, mise-en-space-b9): Vertex-billed sessions write a FULL registry record (name, cwd, tmux coords, status) but the messagingSocketPath field is simply absent — CC itself knows they have no inbox. They are deaf, not dead. sonner currently reports 'no session' for their repo, which is true for delivery but false for a human — and a spawning ring would plant a sibling next to a live busy session.

UPDATE 2026-08-09 evening (sonner-3d): census on tube — 5 of 8 live sessions are deaf (all Vertex-billed), so the invisible class is the MAJORITY, not an edge. Also measured: remote-control (iOS) sessions are never deaf — CC refuses rc under CLAUDE_CODE_USE_VERTEX (api.anthropic.com only), and a live rc child (modha-7a, pid 132601) carries a full record including messagingSocketPath. Deaf class == provider-billed terminal sessions, nothing else observed.
brief.what: 1. Extend live_sessions() or add a deaf_sessions() sweep keyed on the absent-field discriminator 2. Annotate --list 3. Guard spawn with a warning + --force-spawn (or similar) 4. Test with a fixture record lacking messagingSocketPath
brief.done: --list shows the deaf session annotated; a ring at its repo warns instead of silently spawning; fixture test covers the discriminator.
brief.how: The discriminator is the record: messagingSocketPath ABSENT + pid alive = live-but-deaf (provider-gated, e.g. Vertex); socket path present but socket gone = dead. Surface deaf sessions in --list with an annotation (e.g. '[deaf: no inbox — provider-gated]'), and before cold-spawn into a repo holding one, say so and require an explicit flag to spawn anyway.

title: sonner ships as a batterie plugin — CLI plus the peer-messaging skill, fleet-wide

brief.why: Green-lit by Sameer 2026-08-09 with the bon pattern named explicitly: tool+skill repos get their own batterie citizenship. The CLI works installed from source; what remains is the plugin/marketplace layer so every machine gets both the tool and the habits without hand-installing.
brief.what: 1. Add .claude-plugin/plugin.json (copy bon's shape) 2. Register sonner in the batterie-de-savoir marketplace/assembler config 3. Ship a THIN always-on shard (instructions.md -> rules/sonner.md): a few lines naming sonner, the name-[ref] addressing form, and the identical-text silent drop, plus 'invoke Skill(peer-messaging) before SendMessage/sonner work' — Sameer wants near-default loading (2026-08-09), and the bon/mise shard pattern is exactly this 4. Banc pass before fleet-wide default: provenance-style isolated-HOME smevals eval — (a) skill loads on a natural messaging task, (b) does NOT load on adjacent non-messaging tasks (over-trigger control), (c) the addressing rule and wake-or-file test visibly shape behaviour vs a bare arm. The 2026-08-09 subagent test was a live positive but uncontrolled 5. First /batterie:publish; assemble CI green; clean-machine install test 6. Retire ~/.claude/skills/peer-messaging (git rm in spm1001/.claude) in the same change 7. Mac: plugin install once published (CLI already installed + verified there 2026-08-09; skill currently arrives via the .claude clone and step 6 retires that path)
brief.done: claude plugin install sonner@batterie works on a clean machine and brings both CLI wiring and the peer-messaging skill; exactly one copy of the skill exists estate-wide; sonner --list works on tube and the Mac.
brief.how: Follow bon's shape: plugin.json + skills/ shipped via the batterie marketplace assembler (spm1001/batterie). The peer-messaging skill's LIVE copy on tube is ~/.claude/skills/peer-messaging/ — it must be retired in the same change that ships the plugin, or two copies drift. /batterie:publish handles the shard dance once the marketplace knows the plugin; first-time registration is the real work.

title: Derive discovery roots from uid, not caller env

brief.why: son-sotize: from the receptionnaire mail harness (HOME=/srv/receptionnaire/home, XDG_RUNTIME_DIR unset) both discovery paths sweep the wrong places and sonner spawns a duplicate session. The env vars are hints, not ground truth — the uid is.
brief.what: 1. socket_dirs(): add /run/user/<uid>/cc-socks unconditionally, dedupe 2. session_records(): union sweep roots from $HOME and pwd database home 3. Tests for both under a hostile env (HOME elsewhere, XDG unset) 4. Live verify: env -u XDG_RUNTIME_DIR HOME=/foreign sonner --list matches plain sonner --list on tube 5. Reinstall uv tool
brief.done: son-sotize's done: --list under the receptionnaire env names the same sessions as a normal shell; tests cover both discovery roots.
brief.how: Keep env-derived paths as additions (legit overrides), add uid-derived ones unconditionally: /run/user/<os.getuid()>/cc-socks in socket_dirs(), and pwd.getpwuid(os.getuid()).pw_dir as a second sweep root in session_records() alongside Path.home(). Design with the rc/iOS-spawned-session puzzle in view: discovery must not assume anything about the environment the SESSION was born with either — uid-keyed machine truth over inherited env.

steps: session_records(): union sweep roots from $HOME and pwd database home
Tests for both under a hostile env (HOME elsewhere, XDG unset)
Live verify: env -u XDG_RUNTIME_DIR HOME=/foreign sonner --list matches plain sonner --list on tube

title: sonner finds no sessions when HOME isn't /home/modha

brief.why: Rung from the mail inbox (claude@planetmodha.com), sonner reported 'no reachable sessions' while three live sessions with bound sockets were sitting right there, and then timed out spawning a duplicate. Two independent discovery paths both failed for environmental reasons: the receptionnaire harness runs with HOME=/srv/receptionnaire/home, so session_records() sweeps ~/.claude under the wrong home and finds nothing; and XDG_RUNTIME_DIR is unset in that environment, so socket_dirs() never looks in /run/user/1000/cc-socks. Both fallbacks are absent because /tmp/cc-socks exists but is empty on this box. Running with XDG_RUNTIME_DIR=/run/user/1000 set by hand made all three sessions appear immediately. The failure is silent and expensive: it spawns a second session in a repo that already has one, then dies after 180s having delivered nothing.
brief.what: sonner discovers live sessions from the mail inbox environment without an env-var workaround.
brief.done: sonner --list, run with HOME=/srv/receptionnaire/home and XDG_RUNTIME_DIR unset, lists the same sessions it lists from a normal shell.

done_note: Fixed in son-sireto: uid-derived discovery roots (/run/user/<uid>/cc-socks + passwd-database home) added alongside env-derived ones. Verified live: --list under HOME=/srv/receptionnaire/home with XDG_RUNTIME_DIR unset is byte-identical to a normal shell. Receptionnaire has no private sonner copy — the single PATH install is the fixed one.
